name: PlexusCore
headline: One trusted foundation for all of your data
summary: A unified data platform accelerator that stands up ingestion, lakehouse storage, transformation and governance in weeks, not quarters.
description: PlexusCore packages the architecture decisions, infrastructure code and governance patterns from the hundred-plus platform builds our founders led before starting Dataplexor into a deployable foundation. It runs on your cloud, with open table formats and no lock-in, and gives every downstream team — analytics, ML, agents — the same trusted building blocks.

capabilities.title: Ingestion & streaming
capabilities.body: Batch and real-time pipelines with schema enforcement, quality gates and automatic lineage capture at the edge.

capabilities.title: Lakehouse storage
capabilities.body: Open-format lakehouse layout with medallion zoning, time travel and cost-optimized lifecycle policies out of the box.

capabilities.title: Governance & catalog
capabilities.body: Access control, PII classification, data contracts and a searchable catalog wired in from day one — not bolted on later.

capabilities.title: DataOps automation
capabilities.body: CI/CD for pipelines, environment promotion, observability dashboards and freshness SLAs as code.

stats.label: Typical time to a governed production platform
Typical run-cost reduction in consolidations our team has led
Infrastructure as code — portable across AWS, Azure and GCP

faqs.a: In your cloud accounts — AWS, Azure or GCP — deployed as infrastructure as code you own. Nothing routes through our infrastructure, and your data never leaves your tenancy.
Annual subscription covering the platform, upgrades and support, typically bundled with a fixed-fee deployment engagement. No consumption surprises; pricing scales with domains, not rows.

faqs.q: What if we stop using it?
faqs.a: You keep everything. Storage is open table format, pipelines are standard code in your repositories, and infrastructure is Terraform you control. Exit is a decision, not a project.

name: PlexusIQ
headline: From metrics to decisions in one governed layer
summary: A decision-intelligence suite that unifies metrics, ML predictions and natural-language analytics on top of your data platform.
description: PlexusIQ gives your organization a single semantic layer where every metric is defined once and used everywhere — in dashboards, forecasts and conversational analytics. Business users ask questions in plain language; PlexusIQ answers with governed, explainable numbers backed by lineage you can audit.

capabilities.title: Semantic metrics layer
capabilities.body: Version-controlled metric definitions consumed consistently by BI tools, notebooks, APIs and AI assistants.

capabilities.title: Conversational analytics
capabilities.body: Natural-language questions answered from governed metrics — with the SQL, lineage and confidence shown, not hidden.

capabilities.title: Forecasting & ML
capabilities.body: Built-in forecasting, anomaly detection and propensity models that publish predictions back into the metrics layer.

capabilities.title: Decision workflows
capabilities.body: Alerts, approvals and scenario planning that connect insight to the operational systems where decisions execute.

stats.label: Definition per metric, everywhere it is consumed
Of routine reporting questions self-served by business users

faqs.q: Does PlexusIQ replace our BI tools?
faqs.a: No — it feeds them. The semantic layer serves the same governed metrics to your existing BI, notebooks, APIs and the built-in conversational analytics, so adoption starts from the tools people already use.

faqs.q: How does conversational analytics stay trustworthy?
faqs.a: Every answer shows its work: the metric definition used, the generated SQL, the lineage and a confidence signal. Analysts can verify in one click, which is why finance teams sign off on it.
A metrics discovery sprint with your analysts, then the semantic layer built over your existing platform — most clients see their first governed metrics live inside four weeks.

name: AgentMesh
headline: Run AI agents you can actually trust
summary: An orchestration and governance runtime for deploying fleets of AI agents with policy guardrails, observability and human oversight.
description: AgentMesh is the control plane for the agentic enterprise. It lets teams compose agents from models, tools and knowledge; enforces declarative policies on every action; and records complete decision traces. Graduated autonomy means agents earn independence with evidence — and every irreversible action keeps a human hand on the switch.

capabilities.title: Agent orchestration
capabilities.body: Compose single agents or multi-agent workflows with tool access, memory and structured handoffs between agents and humans.

capabilities.title: Policy guardrails
capabilities.body: Declarative rules evaluated on every tool call: permissions, budgets, rate limits and hard stops for irreversible operations.

capabilities.title: Full observability
capabilities.body: Complete traces of inputs, reasoning, actions and outcomes — searchable, auditable and wired to your monitoring stack.

capabilities.title: Evaluation harness
capabilities.body: Continuous regression suites and model-graded scoring so every prompt, model or tool change is proven before release.

stats.label: Of agent actions policy-checked and logged
Average reduction in manual effort on automated workflows

faqs.q: Which model providers does AgentMesh support?
faqs.a: All major providers — Anthropic, OpenAI, the cloud model platforms — plus private deployments. Policy, logging and evaluation sit above the model layer, so you can switch or mix providers without rebuilding governance.

faqs.q: How does AgentMesh satisfy risk and compliance teams?
faqs.a: Declarative policy rules the second line can read and version, complete decision logs retained as a book of record, graduated autonomy with measured reliability, and hard stops on irreversible actions. It was designed with bank validators in the room.

That is the intended path: one workflow, propose-only mode, four to six weeks to a measured baseline — then autonomy expands with evidence. The platform grows from one agent to a governed fleet without re-architecture.
